entry.title: A bitter and failed experience! The prosecutor of Shahriar has announced the…

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

A bitter and failed experience! The prosecutor of Shahriar has announced the arrest of one of the members of the Ferdowsiyeh City Council on charges of bribery! Until a healthy, powerful, and free party system takes shape in the country, council elections not only fail to help improve the administration of the country's cities and villages, but, as has become evident, they add to the scope of corruption and misery. This is while the legal term of the current councils has expired more than a year ago, and the continued activity of the current councils and their elected mayors not only lacks any legal basis, but, given the worsening shortage of resources, increases the level and depth of abuse and corruption. Therefore, at least until the threat to the country is removed and the necessary stability is established, the government should prevent growing corruption in the administration of cities and villages by officially declaring the end of the legal term of the current councils and appointing new mayors by the Ministry of Interior.#Ahmad_Zeydabadi @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at Sharif University of Technology to one of our colleagues, and in fact to the entire body of colleagues at Sharif University of Technology. Its audience is, in reality, all professors and officials of Iranian universities.——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————-We are a group of mothers whose children have, in recent months, faced heavy disciplinary rulings and expulsion from university. We write this letter not out of confrontation, nor to disregard the rules, but from the position of mothers who are worried about the future, the fate, and the lost years of youth of their children, and we have turned to you with great hope. Our children may have made mistakes or committed violations under certain circumstances, and it is natural that the university has the right to react to violations; but is taking away the opportunity to continue education and destroying the future path of a young person the only possible response to a mistake? What pains us most of all is the severity and sometimes irreparability of the punishment that affects the future of these young people. Many of these students have strived for years to get into Sharif University, have completed a significant portion of their studies, and their families have placed all their hope and resources into their future. What is most painful for us is that some of these students, in addition to the disciplinary case at the university and the expulsion ruling, have also faced punishment from the judicial system (mostly one to three years of imprisonment); that is, for a single offense at the university, they have faced two punishments from two institutions—the university and the judicial system! We ask you, if possible, to hear the voice of these mothers and, to the extent of your ability, help in reviewing the expulsion rulings, converting heavy punishments into more proportionate rulings, and providing the possibility for these students to return to the path of education. Sometimes a second chance can save a young person's life. We do not expect you to disregard the law; we only ask that alongside the law, fairness, proportionality of punishment, the circumstances of each student, and the future of a human being also be considered. If you have the means to follow up on these concerns or convey them to university officials or officials of the Ministry of Science, we sincerely request that you do not leave us alone. We thank you in advance for the time you take to hear our voice. With respect and hope, a group of mothers of expelled students of Sharif University of Technology

It was a delightful experience and brought to life in my mind and heart many of the dialogues and atmospheres of the group therapy sessions held over the past five years. After nearly a two-year hiatus, we plan to start a new 15-session "group psychotherapy with an existential approach" course together with dear Dr. Sani from mid-October (around mid-Mehr month), with sessions held on Saturdays at 11 AM North American time, virtually. Friends interested in participating in this group therapy course, given the limited capacity, please message as soon as possible for information and registration at number 4167350042 (code 001) on WhatsApp or on the Instagram page soroush_dabbagh. The therapist-client relationship is like that of two fellow travelers who begin the journey from a specific point and move forward together, but do not know in advance where and at which point the journey will end, for "no one knows what the outcome will be." In my psychotherapy practice over the past nearly six years, I have many times begun, advanced, and completed therapeutic journeys together with clients; experiences that have been instructive and enjoyable in their own right and have greatly aided my self-awareness, self-exploration, and self-knowledge. entry.title: The real innovation of this plan lies in five points: The policy unit shifts…
entry.summary:
Source: @hesmashena

The real innovation of this plan lies in five points: The policy unit shifts from "carrier" to "service." Today, gasoline, gas, electricity, water, and transportation are largely managed in separate platforms. The plan says every decision should be measured based on the final output: "one unit of cooling," "one unit of heating," and "one unit of mobility" — with what combination of resources, technology, and cost they are provided. Four sources and three services are placed in a common decision matrix. For example, replacing gasoline with electricity is only desirable if its effect on the electricity balance, power plant gas, air, and network cost is measured simultaneously. This prevents "transferring imbalance from one carrier to another." Price reform becomes a functional contract rather than a financial measure. The price of excess consumption only rises when a real possibility of reducing consumption has been created; in mobility, that means travel options; in heating, controls and equipment; in cooling, low-consumption technology. This is an operational rule, not a slogan. Instead of buying equipment, the government buys "verified savings." Heaters, coolers, motors, buses, or boiler rooms are not the main subjects of payment. Payment is made against cubic meters of gas, kilowatt-hours of electricity, cubic meters of water, peak megawatts, or actually freed fuel. This change alters the financial and incentive model of the program. Three major consumption markets are redesigned simultaneously and complementarily. In mobility: vehicle–energy–time–cost; in heating: building–equipment–control–behavior; in cooling: electricity–water–peak–comfort. Thus, instead of dozens of scattered projects, three national "savings factories" are formed.

entry.title: This separation prevents the organization from getting bogged down in…
entry.summary:
Source: @hesmashena

This separation prevents the organization from getting bogged down in implementation details and losing its main mission, which is increasing the overall system's productivity. The ultimate success criterion: The program's success should not be measured by the number of heaters, coolers, buses, or motorcycles replaced. The right measure is the amount of service produced with fewer resources. In cooling: reduced electricity, water, and peak demand against maintained comfort. In heating: reduced gas and winter peak against maintained comfort. In mobility: energy consumed per passenger-kilometer or ton-kilometer. At the macro level, the final indicator is: providing more or better cooling, heating, and mobility with less water consumption, less damage to air and soil, less energy, and lower public cost. This framework can transform the organization's 24-month program from a set of scattered projects into a coherent and measurable policy. In this view, gasoline, gas, electricity, coolers, heaters, boiler rooms, and vehicles are not themselves the "problem"; they are tools for providing three main services with higher efficiency and less pressure on the country's four basic resources.
